title: The Stone
logline: A man climbs a smoking volcano through falling ash to return the stone he stole from it as a boy.
look: Black volcanic slopes under a blood-red sky, ash falling like snow, heavy footfalls kicking up ash on every contact; the ending clears to a cold blue dawn.
narrator: male, middle-aged, low pitch, british accent
A weary man confessing, low and close
music: Low drones and slow war drums matched to footfalls, wind and ash hiss; a solo horn at the rim; the drums stop when the stone drops; a held string chord at dawn.

shots.direction: EWS 24mm · slow push · fade in — a black volcano under a red sky, ash falling; a tiny figure at its foot
CU 85mm · hold · cut — a hand holds a smooth black stone
MS low 35mm · tracking · cut — boots step heavily; ash puffs up on every contact
WS 24mm · tracking · cut — he climbs into thickening ash and wind
CU 50mm · shake · cut — he slips and drops to one knee; an ash cloud bursts
MS 50mm · hold · cut — he rests, breathing, and looks at the stone
WS 24mm low angle · tracking · cut — he rises and climbs on
EWS 24mm · slow push · cut — the summit glows ahead
MS 35mm · locked · cut — at the crater rim, he holds the stone up
CU 85mm · locked · cut — he drops it into the crater; a small spark answers
WS 24mm · locked · dissolve — the ash stops falling; the red sky clears to dawn
EWS 24mm · slow pull back · fade out — he sits on the rim, very small, in the first sun

narration.text: When I was nine, I took a stone from this mountain.
They said the mountain would want it back.
For thirty years, it rained ash on our town.
So I am giving it back.
It was never the mountain's anger.
It was mine. And I could put it down.
